title: Orchestra watcher library (orchestra.watchers.json)
description: Declares named watchers: pollers that fetch items from a source on a schedule, deduplicate them per subscriber and launch every orchestration whose trigger references the watcher (trigger.type = watcher). A watcher only runs while at least one enabled orchestration subscribes to it.

$schema.description: Optional pointer to this schema for editor validation.

watchers.description: Map of watcher name to watcher definition. The key is the canonical name used by trigger.watcher references and in state-file names.

propertyNames.description: Watcher name. Any characters are allowed; the name is sanitized for file names.

WatcherEntry.description: A watcher definition. The 'type' discriminator selects how items are fetched: 'poll-command' runs an executable, 'poll-script' runs a script through a shell interpreter.

enabled.description: When false the watcher is never started, even if orchestrations reference it. Subscriptions to a disabled watcher are rejected at registration.

failurePolicy.description: What a failed fetch does: 'warn' logs a warning and keeps polling (with back-off), 'ignore' logs at debug level and keeps polling, 'fail' logs an error and stops this watcher's loop until the host restarts or its subscriptions change.

PollCommandWatcher.description: Runs an executable on every tick. The fetcher protocol payload is written to its stdin; its stdout must be a fetcher-output JSON document.

PollScriptWatcher.description: Runs a script through a shell interpreter (pwsh, bash, python, node, ...) on every tick. The fetcher protocol payload is written to its stdin; its stdout must be a fetcher-output JSON document.

type.description: Discriminator: run a script via a shell interpreter.

arguments.description: Arguments passed to the command or appended after the script path.

workingDirectory.description: Working directory for the child process. Relative paths resolve against the directory containing the file that declares the watcher. Defaults to that directory.

env.description: Environment variables merged on top of the host environment for the child process.

timeoutSeconds.description: Maximum wall-clock time for one fetch. The process is killed on expiry and the tick counts as a failure.

includeStdErr.description: When true, stderr is merged into stdout before JSON parsing. Stderr is always captured and logged on failure regardless of this flag.

config.description: Free-form object passed verbatim to the fetcher as the 'config' field of its stdin payload.

WatcherFetchCommandConfig.description: How to run the fetcher executable.

command.description: Executable name (resolved via PATH) or absolute path.

WatcherFetchScriptConfig.description: How to run the fetcher script. Exactly one of 'scriptFile' or 'script' must be set.

shell.description: Interpreter: pwsh, powershell, bash, sh, python, python3, node, or any executable that accepts a script path as its first argument.

scriptFile.description: Path to the script file. Relative paths resolve against the directory containing the file that declares the watcher. Mutually exclusive with 'script'.

script.description: Inline script body, written to a temporary file for the interpreter. Mutually exclusive with 'scriptFile'.

WatcherSchedule.description: When the watcher polls. Exactly one of 'intervalSeconds' or 'cron' must be set.

intervalSeconds.description: Fixed cadence between ticks, in seconds, measured from the start of the previous tick.

cron.description: Cron expression evaluated in UTC. Standard 5-field (minute precision) or 6-field with a leading seconds field.

WatcherItemsConfig.description: Where the items live inside the fetcher's stdout document. Only needed when the fetcher does not follow the standard protocol shape ({ items: [...] }).

jsonPath.description: Simple JSONPath: '$' root, '.name' / ['name'] member access, '[n]' index and a trailing '[*]' to enumerate an array. Filters and recursive descent are not supported.

WatcherDedup.description: How items are recognised across ticks so each subscriber dispatches once per genuinely new item. If omitted, the default is fifo mode keyed by a hash of the whole item.

key.description: Template producing the dedup key, e.g. '{{item.id}}'. '{{item}}' is the whole item as JSON; missing paths render as the literal 'null'. When omitted the key is a SHA-256 prefix of the item's canonical JSON.

mode.description: 'fifo' remembers the most recent keys (bounded by maxEntries / ttlDays); 'presence' tracks the keys currently visible at the source and forgets a key after it has been absent for graceTicks ticks.

fifo.description: Options for mode = fifo. Not allowed with mode = presence.

maxEntries.description: Maximum remembered keys per subscriber; the oldest are evicted first.

ttlDays.description: Keys older than this are forgotten.

presence.description: Options for mode = presence. Not allowed with mode = fifo.

graceTicks.description: Consecutive ticks a key may be missing before it is forgotten (and would dispatch again if it reappears).
